assumptions: One oscillator with canonical quadratures [q,p]=i; the ideal square-lattice qubit code is the simultaneous +1 generalized eigenspace of S_q and S_p.
Exact ideal stabilizer relations concern distributional, non-normalizable codewords, not normalizable finite-energy approximations.
variables: q,p: canonical quadrature operators; S_q=exp(i2sqrt(pi)q) shifts p by +2sqrt(pi), while S_p=exp(-i2sqrt(pi)p) shifts q by +2sqrt(pi). Subscripts label the quadrature in the exponent, not the shifted coordinate.
patches.units: Dimensionless oscillator quadratures with [q,p]=i (hbar=1); n=2 and alpha=sqrt(pi) in the source. Coefficients and displacement bounds must be rescaled if a different quadrature commutator is used.
patches.regime: The Weyl relation gives S_q S_p=exp(i4pi) S_p S_q=S_p S_q. For ideal syndrome recovery, the central sufficient displacement window is |Delta q|<sqrt(pi)/2 and |Delta p|<sqrt(pi)/2, with both inequalities strict. Half-open modular intervals only choose representatives at boundary ties; they do not guarantee correction of both opposite endpoint errors. This is not an if-and-only-if claim that every larger shift fails.

sourceLocations.locator: Author manuscript arXiv quant-ph/0008040v3 (13 May 2001), Sec. IV, Eq. (21), printed/PDF p. 4; specialize n=2, alpha=sqrt(pi). Canonical commutator and Weyl identity immediately preceding Eq. (23), printed/PDF p. 5.

Sec. IV, Eq. (24), printed/PDF p. 5: strict correctable shift bounds; Sec. V, printed/PDF p. 6, paragraph after Eq. (36): modular syndrome recovery. Boundary-tie qualification is an explicit algebraic consequence, not a quoted source theorem.

patches.theoryRelationship: Existing stabilizer equation checked by direct specialization of the authors' versioned primary manuscript; no equation change. Finite-energy preparations are approximations discussed separately in Sec. V. The existing DOI source remains provenance; these locators refer to the arXiv manuscript, not journal pagination.

assumptions: One oscillator with [q,p]=i; logical action is restricted to the ideal square-GKP qubit code fixed by S_q=exp(i2sqrt(pi)q) and S_p=exp(-i2sqrt(pi)p).
The displayed oscillator displacement operators are unitary; they act as Pauli operators on the ideal code, not as involutions on the entire oscillator Hilbert space.
variables: Z_L: +sqrt(pi) momentum displacement; X_L: +sqrt(pi) position displacement. The logical basis is |j_L> proportional to sum_s |q=(2s+j)sqrt(pi)>, j=0,1.
patches.units: Dimensionless oscillator quadratures with [q,p]=i (hbar=1); n=2 and alpha=sqrt(pi) in the source. Coefficients and displacement bounds must be rescaled if a different quadrature commutator is used.
patches.regime: Z_L X_L=-X_L Z_L by the Weyl phase exp(i pi). Each logical operator commutes with both stabilizer generators, since the cross phases are exp(i2pi)=1. Z_L^2=S_q and X_L^2=S_p, so their squares are identity only on the ideal code. In the formal comb basis, Z_L|j_L>=(-1)^j|j_L> and X_L exchanges |0_L> and |1_L>. Normalizable finite-energy approximations are not exact codewords.

sourceLocations.locator: Author manuscript arXiv quant-ph/0008040v3 (13 May 2001), Sec. IV, Eq. (22), printed/PDF p. 4; Eqs. (23), (26), printed/PDF p. 5. Set n=2 and alpha=sqrt(pi); Eq. (23) then has omega=-1.
Sec. IV, Eq. (21), printed/PDF p. 4, and Eq. (27), printed/PDF p. 5: stabilizer powers and the formal logical basis. Logical-stabilizer commutation follows explicitly from the stated Weyl relation.

patches.theoryRelationship: Existing logical-Pauli equation checked in the authors' versioned primary manuscript, with anticommutation, code-subspace restriction and stabilizer powers made explicit. No equation change; no claim that these are finite-energy exact codewords.

assumptions: One oscillator with [q,p]=i; choose the square qubit code n=2, alpha=sqrt(pi), and logical-zero label j=0 in the source.
Position eigenkets and the infinite equal-weight sum are generalized states/distributions, not normalizable vectors in the oscillator Hilbert space.
variables: s: any integer; |q=q0>: generalized position eigenket. The proportionality sign denotes a formal common amplitude, not an omitted finite normalization constant.
patches.units: Dimensionless oscillator quadratures with [q,p]=i (hbar=1); n=2 and alpha=sqrt(pi) in the source. Coefficients and displacement bounds must be rescaled if a different quadrature commutator is used.
patches.regime: The comb has period 2sqrt(pi) and obeys S_q|0_L>=S_p|0_L>=Z_L|0_L>=|0_L> distributionally. A +sqrt(pi) position shift gives the logical-one comb, rather than the same codeword. The ideal comb is a non-normalizable, formal infinite-energy limit. Finite-width peaks with a decaying envelope, as in Sec. V Eq. (31), are normalizable approximate codewords and must not be substituted into the displayed exact ideal relation without qualification.

sourceLocations.locator: Author manuscript arXiv quant-ph/0008040v3 (13 May 2001), Sec. IV, Eq. (27), printed/PDF p. 5, first line with n=2, alpha=sqrt(pi), j=0; Fig. 1 and the paragraph after Eq. (27) identify the ideal comb and non-normalizability.
Sec. V opening paragraphs and Eqs. (30)-(31), printed/PDF p. 6: finite-width Gaussian peaks and envelope define approximate, normalizable codewords, not the exact ideal comb.
